questions.stem_markdown: The displacement of a particle at time $t$ s after leaving a fixed point $O$ is $s$ m. The diagram shows a displacement-time graph which models the motion of the particle. The graph consists of 4 straight line segments. The particle travels $50$ m in the first $10$ s, then travels at $2$ m s$^{-1}$ for a period of $10$ s. The particle then comes to rest for a period of $20$ s, before returning to its starting point when $t=60$.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the velocity of the particle during the last $20$ s of its motion. [2]
Sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion of the particle from $t=0$ to $t=60$. [3]

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Any explicit expression for the distance, e.g. $$\frac{x-50}{20-10} = 2 \rightarrow x = 2(20-10) + 50$$.
Oe. Ft *their* distance ≠ 50. Must be negative. Do not ISW if (e.g.) velocity = 3.5. Do allow “3.5 m s⁻¹, directed towards O.”
May be seen on diagram.
Stepped diagram with four horizontal lines segments. Ignore vertical line segments.

All correct. 10, 20, 40 and 60 indicated on the t-axis. *Their* 5, 2 and *their* –3.5 (allow –3 and –4 is acceptable too with line segment halfway between them) indicated on the v-axis, corresponding to the position of the horizontal line segments. FT *their* –3.5 m s⁻¹ and/or FT their 5 m s⁻¹. If their answer to (a) is positive, allow use of negative their answer for this mark.

questions.stem_markdown: A particle is projected vertically upwards from horizontal ground. The speed of the particle 2 seconds after it is projected is $5$ m s$^{-1}$ and it is travelling downwards.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the speed of projection of the particle. [2]
Find the distance travelled by the particle between the two times at which its speed is $10$ m s$^{-1}$. [2]

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $$-5 = u - g \times 2$$ or $$5 = u + g \times 2$$ or $$5 = 0 + gt \Rightarrow t = 0.5$$, so time to greatest height is $$T = 2 - 0.5 = 1.5$$. Hence $$0 = u + (-g) \times 1.5$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of constant acceleration to get an equation in $$u$$ only. Using $$v = -5$$, $$t = 2$$ and $$a = \pm g$$.
Must be positive.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $$0^2 = 10^2 - 2gs \quad [\Rightarrow s = 5]$$ or $$10^2 = [0^2 + 2]gs \quad [\Rightarrow s = 5]$$ or $$10 = 0 + gt \Rightarrow t = 1$$, so $$s = 10 \times 1 - \frac{1}{2}g \times 1^2 \quad [\Rightarrow s = 5]$$ or $$\frac{1}{2}(m) \times 10^2 = (m)gh \quad [\Rightarrow h = 5]$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of constant acceleration formula(e) to find distance travelled from height with speed $$10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$$ to maximum height with speed $$0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$$, $$a = \pm g$$. Must be a complete method, e.g. $$0^2 = (\text{their } 15)^2 - 2gs_1 \quad [\Rightarrow s_1 = 11.25]$$ and $$10^2 = (\text{their } 15)^2 - 2gs_2 \quad [\Rightarrow s_2 = 6.25]$$ or $$10 = (\text{their } 15) - gt \quad [\Rightarrow t = 0.5]$$, $$s_2 = \frac{1}{2}(\text{their } 15 + 10) \times (\text{their } 0.5)$$ and with an attempt at $$s_1 - s_2 = 5$$. Energy method with 2 terms, dimensionally correct.
FT $$\text{their } 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$$ if used.

The plane is inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal and the rope is parallel to the plane. The winch is working at a constant rate of $8$ kW.

Find the coefficient of friction between the crate and the plane. [5]

questions.stem_markdown:
A particle moves in a straight line starting from a point $O$. The velocity $v$ m s$^{-1}$ of the particle $t$ s after leaving $O$ is given by

$$v=t^3-\frac{9}{2}t^2+1 \text{ for } 0\leq t\leq 4.$$

You may assume that the velocity of the particle is positive for $t<\frac{1}{2}$, is zero at $t=\frac{1}{2}$ and is negative for $t>\frac{1}{2}$.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the distance travelled between $t=0$ and $t=\frac{1}{2}$. [4]
Find the positive value of $t$ at which the acceleration is zero. Hence find the total distance travelled between $t=0$ and this instant. [4]

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Increase power by 1 and a change in coefficient in at least one term (which must be the same term). $$s = vt$$ is M0.
May be unsimplified.
Use limits 0 and $$\frac{1}{2}$$ correctly, or substitute $$t = \frac{1}{2}$$. M0 if including other regions.
Decrease power by 1 and a change in coefficient in at least one term (which must be the same term). $$a = \frac{v}{t}$$ is M0.
Ignore $$t = 0$$ if not rejected.

Must be using an expression for s from integration. Allow missing minus sign at start; use limits $$\frac{1}{2}$$ and their 3 correctly, where $$\frac{1}{2} < \text{their } 3 \le 4$$. Or use limit 3 and find difference from $$\text{their } \frac{21}{64}$$ from part (a). May see $$2 \times \left( \frac{1}{4} \times \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^4 - \frac{3}{2} \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^3 + \left( \frac{1}{2} \right) \right) - \left( \frac{1}{4} \times 3^4 - \frac{3}{2} \times 3^3 + 3 \right)$$

Oe, e.g. $$\frac{573}{32}$$, 17.90625. Condone 17.9. FT $$\text{their}$$ positive integration value in part (a), e.g. $$17 \frac{37}{64} + \text{their (a)}$$ or $$\frac{69}{4} + 2 \times \text{their (a)}$$.
Decrease power by 1 and a change in coefficient in at least one term (which must be the same term). $$a = \frac{v}{t}$$ is M0.

questions.stem_markdown: A car of mass $1800$ kg is towing a trailer of mass $300$ kg up a straight road inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha=0.05$. The car and trailer are connected by a tow-bar which is light and rigid and is parallel to the road. There is a resistance force of $800$ N acting on the car and a resistance force of $F$ N acting on the trailer. The driving force of the car's engine is $3000$ N.

parts.prompt_markdown:
It is given that $F=100$.

Find the acceleration of the car and the tension in the tow-bar. [5]

It is given instead that the total work done against $F$ in moving a distance of $50$ m up the road is $6000$ J. The speed of the car at the start of the $50$ m is $20\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

Use an energy method to find the speed of the car at the end of the $50$ m. [5]

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Attempt at Newton’s second law on car or trailer or system
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Correct number of terms; allow sign errors; allow sin/cos mix; $$\sin \alpha$$ or $$\alpha = 2.865\dots$$ needs to be substituted; allow with $$\alpha = 2.87$$ or $$2.9$$ or better; allow $$g$$ missing.
Any two equations correct.
From equations with correct number of relevant terms, allow $$g$$ missing. If no working seen, must be correct for their equations.
Oe. Allow 0.499 from $$\alpha = 2.87$$.
Allow awrt 400 to 3sf, www. Condone using car equation with 0.499 to get $$T = 400.5$$. Using exact $$a$$ from an inexact angle gives $$T = 400$$.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Work done against resistance on car = $$800 \times 50 [= 40000]$$ or Work done by driving force = $$3000 \times 50 [= 150000]$$

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Allow $$2100g \times 50 \times \sin 2.9$$. Or $$2100g \times 50 \times \sin 2.87$$.

Attempt at work-energy equation; correct number of relevant terms; dimensionally correct; allow sign errors; allow sin/cos mix in relevant resolved terms. Only PE must be from a component. Allow $$2100g \times 50 \times \sin 2.9$$ or $$2100g \times 50 \times \sin 2.87$$.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Work done against resistance on car = $$800 \times 50 [= 40000]$$ or Work done by driving force = $$3000 \times 50 [= 150000]$$ or Work done against tension = $$\frac{2920}{7} \times 50 [= \frac{146000}{7}]$$

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Or $$300g \times 50 \times 0.05 [= 7500]$$. Allow $$1800g \times 50 \times \sin 2.9$$ or $$1800g \times 50 \times \sin 2.87$$. Or $$\frac{1}{2} \times 300 \times 20^2 [60000]$$.

Attempt at work-energy equation; correct number of relevant terms; dimensionally correct; allow sign errors; allow sin/cos mix in relevant resolved terms. Only PE must be from a component. M0 if using $$T$$ from part (a).
